title: Promotion and en passant
line: A pawn on the last rank becomes a queen or another piece; the one capture that lands behind a pawn.

steps.text: A pawn that reaches the last rank, the far row, must become another piece: a queen, a rook, a bishop or a knight.
Push the pawn to e8 and make it a queen.

wrong.e7e8n: A knight is allowed, but a lone knight can never give checkmate. A queen is far stronger.
wrong.e7e8b: A bishop is allowed, but a lone bishop can never give checkmate.

also.e7e8r: A rook is allowed too, and it wins here. Most players choose the queen, the strongest piece.

steps.after: The pawn is now a queen. Most players choose the queen, the strongest piece.

steps.text: A pawn can also capture its way onto the last row. Capture the rook and make a queen.
steps.hint: The pawn captures one square diagonally forward.
steps.after: The pawn took the rook and became a queen in the same move.

steps.text: Black moves a pawn two squares, from d7 to d5, and lands right beside your pawn on e5.
Your pawn may capture it as if it had moved only one square. Capture en passant: move to d6.

wrong.e5e6: That moves the pawn ahead and leaves the pawn on d5 alone. Capture it by moving to d6.

steps.hint: Move your pawn diagonally forward, to the ringed empty square.
steps.after: The black pawn is gone, though your pawn did not land on its square.

steps.text: This capture is called en passant, French for in passing. It is allowed only on the move right after the two-square step.

summary: A pawn that reaches the last row becomes a queen or another piece. En passant takes a pawn that just passed by.
